answer: The system resists Sybil attacks by behavioral clustering: identities whose answers arrive within 2 seconds of each other on 9 of 10 tasks are grouped and earn weight only as one identity. Each identity in a group completes a route to earn its own weight: it crosses a 100-meter bridge, waits 6 hours at an oasis relay point, then descends 300 meters to a canyon relay point, with timestamps at least 6 hours apart. Timestamps and device signatures must match that identity alone, so one route cannot free two identities and 50 fakes need 50 routes and 300 waiting hours.
